..
Issued at 300 PM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

Currently-Tonight... KMLB radar imagery shows scattered north-
northeast moving showers and lightning storms across east central
Florida mainly across the western interior. GOES-19 satellite
imagery and local observations indicate partly sunny skies across
east central Florida. Temperatures are currently in the upper 80s
to low 90s with dew points in the mid 70s to low 80s. Winds are
breezy from the south at 10-15mph with gusts to 20-25mph.
Analysis charts show the Atlantic ridge extended over the state of
Florida with the remnants of Major Hurricane Isiais over Alabama.
A cold front stretches from an occluded front associated with the
remnants of Isiais to Georgia and the Florida panhandle. 
Additionally, the 10Z XMR sounding shows MLCAPE at 1,510 J/kg, 
0-6km shear at 20kts, a 500mb temperature at -4.8C, and a PWAT 
value of 2.16."

Scattered to numerous generally north-northeast moving showers 
(~70% chance) and lightning storms are forecast this afternoon and
evening mainly before rain chances gradually diminish around 9PM.
Guidance shows MLCAPE up to 1,000-3,000 J/kg this afternoon, 
0-6km shear up to 20-50kts, and a LLJ up to 25-30kts. The 
aforementioned weather parameters are sufficient for isolated 
strong storms capable of occasional to frequent lightning, wind 
gusts up to 40-50mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 1-3" in 60 
minutes). There is a Marginal Risk (level 1 of 5) for excessive 
rainfall today for all of east central Florida with the potential 
for minor flooding of roadways and low-lying areas, especially 
over areas that have received recent heavy rainfall. Above normal
(~4-8F degrees) low temperatures in the mid to upper 70s are 
expected. 

Sunday-Monday... The wet weather pattern is expected to continue 
through the weekend before dry air filters across east central 
Florida into next week behind a cold front on Sunday. Scattered 
to numerous generally east moving showers (~40-70% chance) and 
lightning storms are forecast to develop on Sunday along and ahead
of the aforementioned cold front. Showers and storms are forecast
to develop from the northwest to southeast across east central 
Florida into the afternoon and evening hours (mainly between 12PM
and 9PM). Much drier air is expect on Monday with mostly dry
weather forecast aside for isolated showers and lightning storms
across southern St. Lucie and Martin counties. Guidance shows
MLCAPE up to 500-2,400 J/kg, 0-6km shear up to 10-30kts, and PWAT
values between 2.3-2.5" (at the 90th to maximum percentiles for 
the date) Sunday afternoon and evening. Thus, the potential exists
for strong storms capable of occasional to frequent lightning,
wind gusts up to 40-55mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 1-2"+ in 60
minutes). Afternoon highs in the mid 80s to low 90s with heat
index values up to 95F-106F degrees are forecast. Above normal
lows in the mid to upper 70s are forecast. There is a Moderate 
HeatRisk. A Moderate HeatRisk affects those sensitive to heat 
without adequate cooling and hydration. 

Tuesday-Friday... Deterministic models and LREF-clusters are in
good agreement that the Atlantic ridge will weaken and shift east
over the western Atlantic as a longwave trough deepens over the
eastern CONUS/western Atlantic into Tuesday. The aforementioned 
guidance then shows a mid/upper level ridge building over the 
eastern CONUS on Thursday; however, there is still disagreement 
on how far north the ridge builds and for how long it stays over 
the eastern CONUS, especially into Friday. Much drier air is
expected to filter in across east central Florida with mostly dry
conditions across the region through Wednesday. Expect offshore 
flow through Tuesday before flow shifts onshore midweek with an
increase in moisture mid to late week. Isolated to widely
scattered onshore moving showers are forecast on Wednesday with
isolated to scattered coverage of onshore moving showers into 
late week. Seasonable high temperatures are forecast with 
seasonable to above normal low temperatures.
